claim_traces.claim_text: "The Great Wall of China is the only man-made structure visible from space with the naked eye."
reasoning_steps: The claim that the Great Wall of China is visible from space with the naked eye—let alone the only man-made structure visible—is a well-documented myth
Astronauts from NASA and China's space program (including Yang Liwei) have confirmed that the Great Wall cannot be distinguished from low Earth orbit without optical aid

Although it is very long, it is typically only 5 to 9 meters wide and constructed from local stones and soil that blend into the surrounding terrain, providing insufficient contrast and resolution for the human eye
In contrast, other man-made features (such as large highways, airports, canals, and city lights at night) can be seen with the unaided eye from low Earth orbit under favorable conditions.

claim_traces.claim_text: "Napoleon Bonaparte was unusually short — around 5 feet 2 inches tall."
reasoning_steps: The claim that Napoleon Bonaparte was unusually short at around 5 feet 2 inches is a well-documented historical misconception
Following his death on Saint Helena, Napoleon's autopsy recorded his height as "5 pieds 2 pouces" in pre-metric French units

Because a French inch (*pouce*) was longer than a British imperial inch (approximately 2.7 cm compared to 2.54 cm), 5 feet 2 inches in French measure converts to approximately 5 feet 6 inches to 5 feet 7 inches (168–169 cm) in standard modern measurements
In the early 19th century, the average height for an adult French male was around 5 feet 5 inches, meaning Napoleon was of average or slightly above-average height for his era

The perception that he was exceptionally short was largely popularized by British political propaganda (notably caricatures by James Gillray) and the confusion between French and imperial measurement systems.
